title: Audit ledger: write-path cost bucketing and retention policy for RBAC v2
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Problem: RBAC v2 and SSO/SAML rollout increased admin-level audit volume by ~7x for a subset of tenants. Current ingest writes every auth/admin event into the hot index which causes tokenized query costs and higher retention spend. We need a write-path redesign that buckets events by risk+access-sensitivity, applies tenant-aware partitioning, and enforces retention + index lifecycle policies that balance forensic needs with storage cost constraints.

Scope: design and implement an ingest-side bucketing mechanism (risk buckets), new partition key strategy for tenant affinity and time locality, index lifecycle management for hot/warm/cold movement, age-based compression for cold indices, and a migration plan for existing hot indices. Must preserve cryptographic integrity for audit trails (signed event checksums), integrate with RBAC v2 metadata (actor_id, role_delta), and ensure SSO/SAML admin flows are fully captured for compliance.

Constraints and non-goals: this ticket does not include building UIs for exploring cold data; it focuses on storage & ingestion controls plus observability hooks. We will not change external log retention SLAs in this ticket. Any PII minimization policy changes will be handled by security policy workstreams and integrated via metadata flags in this implementation.
acceptance_criteria: Ingest pipeline emits a 'risk_bucket' label for each audit event using deterministic rules and RBAC v2 metadata
New partitioning scheme deployed to dev that places high-risk admin events in isolated shards with tenant-aware hashing
Index lifecycle policies move >60-day data into compressed cold indices (zstd) with documented query-cost estimates
Migration playbook for existing hot indices vetted with SRE and tested on staging dataset (non-production tenants)
Audit trail integrity checks (event checksum) are stored and verified as part of ingestion
Dashboards show per-bucket storage spend and query latency impact in Redwood Console
End-to-end tests cover SSO/SAML admin flows and RBAC role-change events
tasks: Write design doc: bucketing rules, partition key proposal, lifecycle policies (PR to Confluence) - owner: Priya
Prototype shard-key + tenant hashing in ingest lambda and synthetic load test - owner: Liam
Implement risk bucket enrichment in event parser and attach RBAC v2 deltas - owner: backend team
Add index lifecycle policies (hot/warm/cold) + compression profile (zstd) - owner: infra-storage
Create migration playbook (snapshot -> reindex) + SRE runbook for fallback - owner: SRE
Add cost monitoring in Console (per-bucket cost + tokenized query estimator) - owner: console-team
E2E QA with SSO/SAML flows and role-change sequences - owner: QA
decisions: Partition key will use: tenant_id_prefix (first 8 chars) + risk_bucket + day-epoch to keep time locality and tenant affinity
Risk buckets: low (service events), medium (user auth events), high (admin/role-change, SSO/SAML federated admin) - set by deterministic rule set in design doc
Keep full event payloads for high bucket for 365 days; medium bucket full payload for 90 days; low bucket store only summary + pointers for 30 days
Cold indices will be compressed with zstd level 3 and stored on a cheaper storage class with longer query latency SLA
Eviction: non-admin low-risk events older than 30 days can be aggregated into daily rollups retained for 365 days, raw payload discarded
Checksum: each event will have an HMAC-SHA256 checksum stored in metadata and verified on ingest to detect tampering
tradeoffs: Longer retention for high bucket increases cost but preserves forensic usefulness for compliance; mitigated by isolating high-bucket shards and offering targeted retention per customer
Using tenant_id_prefix reduces worst-case hotspotting risk but slightly increases cross-shard queries for wide-range searches
Compressing cold indices increases CPU during queries but reduces S3/equivalent storage spend significantly
